text:
maya: Quick announcement — we’re planning a company-wide migration from Jira -> GitHub Issues for all product, infra, and platform projects. Full migration doc: https://redwood-internal/repo/devex/jira-to-gh-issues (TL;DR below).

maya: Key dates: export dry-run next Tue 2026-05-05, read-only freeze starts 2026-05-12 00:00 UTC, cutover and final import 2026-05-15 02:00–06:00 UTC. Expect ~4h downtime for writes across Jira.

liam: Will links to old tickets keep working? attachments?

maya: Links: we’ll keep a redirector service so old jira URLs will 301 -> new GH issue pages for common patterns. Attachments will be copied to our S3 bucket and referenced in the migrated issue body. There will be a mapping table in the migration doc.

jen: Who’s running the import? and what about automations / Jira workflows?

maya: DevEx + Eng-Infra will run the import. Automations need manual review — Jira workflows won’t translate 1:1. We’ll map critical automations (eg: severity tags, sprint -> milestone) and provide new GH Actions + issue templates to replicate behavior. Non-critical custom rules will be frozen and flagged for manual rebuild.

deploy-bot: Migration tool (issue-migrate v1.2) dry-run started by @maya at 1807505400 — 1200 issues scanned, 3 parse warnings.

alex: For CI hooks: where do we update pipelines that reference JIRA issue keys?

maya: Pipeline owners need to replace JIRA-specific API calls with GitHub Issues API/webhooks. Example curl to create a GH issue from CI:```
curl -s -H "Authorization: token $GITHUB_TOKEN" 
  -d '{"title":"Bug: failing e2e on main","body":"Original Jira: https://jira/..."}' 
  https://api.github.com/repos/redwood/my-repo/issues
```

maya: We’ve added a helper action in actions/utils to normalize old issue-key references -> issue URLs. We’ll publish a migration PR template you can drop into workflows.

samir: SCIM / SSO question: will project permissions map automatically?

maya: We’ll map Jira project roles -> GitHub teams via an intermediate mapping file. SCIM provisioning stays the same; GitHub org team sync will be configured during cutover. Some edge-case roles (Jira Service Desk admins) will need manual assignment post-migration.

olivia: What about historical reports & exports (velocity, burndown)?

maya: Historical sprint metrics will be exported as CSVs and stored in /reports/jira-archive/; we’ll provide scripts to re-generate common charts. We recommend teams export any ad-hoc dashboards they rely on before the freeze.

jen: Freeze window will break some runbooks — ops needs notice. Can we shorten the write freeze for critical services?

maya: We can keep emergency edits via a tracked process (submit an "Emergency Issue Edit" ticket to #eng-oncall, will be carefully applied by Eng-Infra). Please add any runbooks that require exceptions to the migration doc checklist by EOD Friday.

liam: I can help validate converted issues for the product org. samir too.

samir: yep, happy to spot-check a few projects (esp. infra and infra-internal).

maya: Awesome — volunteers noted. Next steps: 1) read migration doc, 2) opt-in slot for spot-checks (link in doc), 3) join dry-run sync Tue 10:00 UTC. Sync invite will go out. :calendar: :rocket: 

maya: If you have specific pipelines or automations that absolutely must be preserved, tag them in the doc under "preserve" with a short justification. We’ll triage this week.

alex: Thanks — will start listing workflows that use JIRA_API_TOKEN.

jen: heads-up to product managers — we’ll need to reconfirm component mappings and labels.

maya: Yep — product PMs please review the labels mapping section. Contact me or @olivia for permissions questions.

olivia: pinged security/identity to review the SCIM mapping, will report back with any blockers by Monday.

maya: Thanks everyone. Will post migration run logs to this thread during dry-run. :thumbsup:
